Keywords: await, early return, branch, wasted fetch, server component, async
Description: An await at the top of a function stops everything below it, even branches that never use the result.
Do: Move the await into the branch that needs the data, and return early for the cheap case first.
Don't: Do not await a value you only read inside one if-block.

Keywords: Promise.all, parallel fetch, waterfall, sequential await, server component
Description: Two awaits in a row run one after the other. If the second does not need the first, the page waits for both times added together.
Do: Start independent requests at once and await them together.
Don't: Do not chain awaits for data that does not depend on each other.
Code Example Good: const [user, orders] = await Promise.all([getUser(id), getOrders(id)]);
Code Example Bad:
const user = await getUser(id);
const orders = await getOrders(id);

Keywords: start promise, preload pattern, partial dependency, dependent data
Description: When one request needs another's result but a third does not, begin the independent one right away instead of queuing it behind.
Do: Create the promises up front, then await each at the point of use.
Don't: Do not place the independent fetch after an unrelated await.

Keywords: Suspense, streaming, fallback, loading ui, slow data, progressive render
Description: A slow query held in the page body blocks everything. A Suspense boundary lets the rest stream out first.
Do: Put the slow component inside Suspense with a fallback shaped like the result.
Don't: Do not make the whole route wait on its slowest widget.
Code Example Good:
<Suspense fallback={<ReviewsSkeleton />}>
  <Reviews productId={id} />
</Suspense>
Code Example Bad:
const reviews = await getReviews(id); // blocks the whole page
return <Page reviews={reviews} />;

Keywords: parallel routes, layout and page, fetch in each component, waterfall across segments
Description: Fetching in a parent and again in a child, each awaited, chains round trips down the tree.
Do: Fetch where the data is used, use cached helpers so repeats are free, and avoid awaiting a parent's data before rendering a child that doesn't need it.
Don't: Do not pass awaited data down only to fetch more with it.
Code Example Good:
// layout.js and page.js each call getUser(); cache() makes the second call free
const user = await getUser();
Code Example Bad: // layout awaits user, then page awaits orders, then widget awaits stats, in series

Issue: Import from the module you need
Keywords: barrel file, tree shaking, optimizePackageImports, icon library, large import
Description: Importing from an index file that re-exports hundreds of modules can pull them all into the build and slow dev start.
Do: Import the specific file or enable the framework's package import optimisation for big libraries.
Don't: Do not import one icon from a barrel that re-exports thousands.
Code Example Bad: import { Camera } from 'giant-icon-library';

Keywords: next/dynamic, lazy loading, code splitting, ssr false, chart, editor
Description: A rich editor or chart library can double the first download although most visits never open it.
Do: Load it with dynamic import when it is about to be shown.
Don't: Do not bundle a rarely used panel into the entry chunk.
Code Example Good:
import dynamic from 'next/dynamic'; const Editor = dynamic(() => import('./Editor'), { loading: () =>

Loading editor

});
Code Example Bad: import Editor from './Editor'; // loaded for every visitor

Keywords: lazy, Suspense, code split, client component, route split
Description: React.lazy defers a component's code until first render, which suits panels behind a click or tab.
Do: Wrap lazily loaded components in Suspense and keep the fallback small.
Don't: Do not call lazy inside a component body; it must sit at module level.
Code Example Good:
const Chart = lazy(() => import('./Chart'));
<Suspense fallback={<Spinner />}>{open && <Chart />}</Suspense>
Code Example Bad: function Panel() { const Chart = lazy(() => import('./Chart')); return <Chart />; }

Keywords: next/script, afterInteractive, lazyOnload, analytics, chat widget, tag manager
Description: Analytics and chat widgets compete with your own code for the main thread and the network at the most sensitive moment.
Do: Load them with next/script and a strategy that waits until the page is interactive or idle.
Don't: Do not place blocking script tags in the head for non-essential tools.
Code Example Good:
import Script from 'next/script';
<Script src='https://example.com/widget.js' strategy='lazyOnload' />
Code Example Bad: <script src='https://example.com/widget.js'></script>

Keywords: feature flag, dynamic import, admin only, conditional module, role
Description: Code behind a flag or a role is dead weight for everyone who cannot reach it.
Do: Import it inside the condition so only people who get the feature download it.
Don't: Do not statically import admin tooling in a public page.
Code Example Good: if (user.isAdmin) { const { AdminTools } = await import('./admin-tools'); mount(AdminTools); }
Code Example Bad: import { AdminTools } from './admin-tools';

Issue: Prefetch what the visitor is about to open
Keywords: Link prefetch, intent, hover, preload, navigation, next/link
Description: Fetching the next page's code and data before the click makes navigation feel instant.
Do: Use the framework's Link component, which prefetches routes that scroll into view in production, and turn it off only for huge unlikely targets.
Don't: Do not use plain anchors for internal navigation in an app router site.
Code Example Good:
import Link from 'next/link';
<Link href='/pricing'>Pricing</Link>
Code Example Bad: Pricing

Keywords: use client, server component, leaf component, client boundary, interactive island
Description: A 'use client' line makes that file and everything it imports ship to the browser.
Do: Put it on the smallest interactive leaf, such as a like button, and leave the surrounding page as a server component.
Don't: Do not mark a layout or a whole page as client for one onClick.
Code Example Bad: 'use client'; // at the top of page.jsx, so all of it ships

Keywords: React cache, request memoization, same data twice, getUser, server component
Description: Two components that ask for the same record in one request would run the query twice.
Do: Wrap the data function in cache so repeat calls within one render share the result.
Don't: Do not thread props through five layers just to avoid a second query.
Code Example Good:
import { cache } from 'react';
export const getUser = cache(async (id) => db.user.find(id));
Code Example Bad: export async function getUser(id) { return db.user.find(id); } // called in layout and page

Keywords: fetch cache, revalidate, ISR, stale, data cache, time based
Description: Data that changes hourly does not need rebuilding for every visitor.
Do: Set a revalidation time on fetch, or tag the data and revalidate on change.
Don't: Do not leave a slow third-party call uncached on a hot route.
Code Example Good: const res = await fetch(url, { next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['prices'] } });
Code Example Bad: const res = await fetch(url, { cache: 'no-store' }); // every visit hits the API

Keywords: serialization, props, rsc payload, large object, select fields
Description: Everything you pass from a server component to a client one is serialised into the page.
Do: Pass only the fields the client needs.
Don't: Do not hand over a whole database row or a big array for one label.
Code Example Good: <Profile name={user.name} avatar={user.avatarUrl} />
Code Example Bad: <Profile user={user} /> // includes the whole record and its relations

Issue: Fetch in parallel on the server
Keywords: parallel data fetching, Promise.all, server component, multiple sources
Description: Data sources in one server component should load together.
Do: Gather them with Promise.all or split into sibling components that each fetch.
Don't: Do not sequence unrelated reads.
Code Example Good: const [posts, tags] = await Promise.all([getPosts(), getTags()]);
Code Example Bad: const posts = await getPosts(); const tags = await getTags();

Keywords: after, logging, analytics, background task, non-blocking, response time
Description: Logging and analytics should not hold up the reply.
Do: Schedule them with after so they run once the response has been sent.
Don't: Do not await a log write before returning.
Code Example Good:
import { after } from 'next/server';
export async function POST(req) { after(() => logEvent('signup')); return Response.json({ ok: true }); }
Code Example Bad: export async function POST(req) { await logEvent('signup'); return Response.json({ ok: true }); }

Issue: Mutate with server actions and revalidate
Keywords: server action, revalidatePath, form action, mutation, refresh data
Description: After a change, cached pages that show the old data must be refreshed or people see stale content.
Do: Use a server action and call revalidatePath or revalidateTag for the affected data.
Don't: Do not refetch the whole app in the browser after each change.
Code Example Bad: await fetch('/api/todos', { method: 'POST' }); location.reload();

Keywords: server action security, authorization, input validation, public endpoint
Description: A server action is a public HTTP endpoint. Hiding the button does not protect it.
Do: Check who is calling and validate the input inside the action.
Don't: Do not trust a client-side check.
Code Example Good:
'use server';
export async function remove(id) { const s = await getSession(); if (!s?.canEdit) throw new Error('forbidden'); await db.remove(Number(id)); }
Code Example Bad:
'use server';
export async function remove(id) { await db.remove(id); }

Keywords: useEffect fetch, race condition, ignore flag, loading state, data library
Description: A fetch in an effect starts after render and can return out of order, showing the wrong result.
Do: Fetch on the server, or use a data library; if you must use an effect, ignore stale responses in cleanup.
Don't: Do not set state from a response without checking it is still wanted.
Code Example Bad: useEffect(() => { fetchUser(id).then(setUser); }, [id]);

Keywords: event listener, cleanup function, memory leak, addEventListener, subscription
Description: A listener added in an effect and never removed piles up with each render or mount.
Do: Return a cleanup that removes it, with the same function reference.
Don't: Do not add a window listener in the component body.
Code Example Bad: useEffect(() => { window.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => close()); }, []);

Keywords: useSyncExternalStore, subscribe, tearing, browser api, online status
Description: State that lives outside React, like the connection status, needs a subscription React understands to stay consistent.
Do: Use useSyncExternalStore with a subscribe function and a server snapshot.
Don't: Do not mirror external state into useState with an effect.
Code Example Good: const online = useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, () => navigator.onLine, () => true);
Code Example Bad: const [online, setOnline] = useState(true); useEffect(() => { setOnline(navigator.onLine); }, []);

Issue: Read state where it is used
Keywords: state colocation, lift down, prop drilling, unnecessary rerender
Description: State kept high in the tree re-renders everything beneath it on each change.
Do: Move state down into the component that actually uses it.
Don't: Do not keep a typing buffer in the page root.
Code Example Good: function Search() { const [q, setQ] = useState(''); return <input value={q} onChange={e => setQ(e.target.value)} />; }
Code Example Bad: function Page() { const [q, setQ] = useState(''); return <><Search q={q} setQ={setQ} /><HeavyChart /></>; }

Keywords: memo, props equal, expensive child, React.memo, compiler
Description: A costly child re-renders when its parent does, even with identical props.
Do: Wrap it in memo when its props are stable, or let the React Compiler do this.
Don't: Do not wrap every component; measure first.
Code Example Good: const Chart = memo(function Chart({ data }) { return <canvas /* draws data */ />; });
Code Example Bad: function Chart({ data }) { return <canvas />; } // redraws on every parent keystroke

Keywords: useEffect dependencies, object identity, primitive deps, infinite loop
Description: An object or function created in render is new each time and re-runs an effect that depends on it.
Do: Depend on primitives, or move the object inside the effect.
Don't: Do not silence the lint rule to stop a loop.
Code Example Good: useEffect(() => { connect({ room }); }, [room]);
Code Example Bad: const opts = { room }; useEffect(() => { connect(opts); }, [opts]);

Keywords: derived state, computed value, redundant state, sync bug
Description: A value you can compute from props or state does not need its own state; copies drift apart.
Do: Calculate it during render.
Don't: Do not set derived data in an effect.
Code Example Good: const visible = todos.filter(t => !t.done);
Code Example Bad: const [visible, setVisible] = useState([]); useEffect(() => setVisible(todos.filter(t => !t.done)), [todos]);

Keywords: setState updater, stale closure, previous state, batch
Description: Reading state in a handler can use an old snapshot when several updates are queued.
Do: Pass an updater function when the new value depends on the old.
Don't: Do not call setCount(count + 1) twice and expect two increments.
Code Example Good: setCount(c => c + 1); setCount(c => c + 1);
Code Example Bad: setCount(count + 1); setCount(count + 1);

Keywords: useState initializer, expensive init, localStorage read, JSON parse
Description: An expensive expression passed to useState runs on every render, though only the first value is used.
Do: Pass a function so it runs once.
Don't: Do not call the loader in the argument.
Code Example Good: const [items] = useState(() => JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('items') ?? '[]'));
Code Example Bad: const [items] = useState(JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('items') ?? '[]'));

Keywords: useTransition, startTransition, urgent vs non urgent, filter, slow render
Description: A heavy list update triggered by typing blocks the input.
Do: Mark the slow update as a transition so typing stays urgent.
Don't: Do not wrap the controlled input value itself.
Code Example Good:
const [pending, start] = useTransition();
<input value={text} onChange={e => { setText(e.target.value); start(() => setFilter(e.target.value)); }} />
Code Example Bad: <input onChange={e => setFilter(e.target.value)} /> // 10,000 rows re-render per key

Keywords: useDeferredValue, stale ui, debounce alternative, expensive child
Description: A child that is slow to render can lag behind a fast value without blocking it.
Do: Pass a deferred copy of the value to the slow child.
Don't: Do not add timers to emulate debounce for rendering.
Code Example Good:
const deferred = useDeferredValue(query);
return <Results query={deferred} />;
Code Example Bad: const [d, setD] = useState(''); useEffect(() => { const t = setTimeout(() => setD(query), 300); return () => clearTimeout(t); }, [query]);

Keywords: key prop, list rendering, index key, reorder, state loss
Description: Index keys make React reuse the wrong component when items are inserted or reordered.
Do: Use a stable id from the data as the key.
Don't: Do not generate keys with Math.random during render.
Code Example Good: {todos.map(t => <TodoRow key={t.id} todo={t} />)}
Code Example Bad: {todos.map((t, i) => <TodoRow key={i} todo={t} />)}

Keywords: context value, provider, consumers rerender, useMemo value
Description: Every consumer re-renders when the value of a context changes, even for parts it ignores.
Do: Memoise the value, and split rarely and often changing data into separate contexts.
Don't: Do not create the value object inline on each render.
Code Example Good:
const value = useMemo(() => ({ user, logout }), [user, logout]);
<AuthContext value={value}>{children}</AuthContext>
Code Example Bad: <AuthContext value={{ user, logout }}>{children}</AuthContext>

Keywords: useMemo, expensive computation, filter large array, console.time
Description: Sorting or filtering thousands of items on every render wastes time when the inputs have not changed.
Do: Cache the result with useMemo, after measuring that it is slow.
Don't: Do not use it for trivial maths.
Code Example Good: const sorted = useMemo(() => [...rows].sort(byDate), [rows]);
Code Example Bad: const sorted = [...rows].sort(byDate); // runs on every keystroke elsewhere

Keywords: useCallback, function identity, memo child, handler
Description: A new function each render defeats memo on the child that receives it.
Do: Wrap handlers passed to memoised children in useCallback.
Don't: Do not add it where nothing is memoised.
Code Example Good:
const onSave = useCallback((d) => save(id, d), [id]);
<Form onSave={onSave} />
Code Example Bad: <Form onSave={(d) => save(id, d)} /> // Form is memo, so this breaks it

Keywords: constant jsx, module scope, static element, icons
Description: Markup that never changes is rebuilt on every render if it sits inside the component.
Do: Define it once at module level.
Don't: Do not recreate large unchanging trees.
Code Example Good:
const divider = <hr className='my-4' />;
function Card() { return <>{divider}</>; }
Code Example Bad: function Card() { return <><hr className='my-4' /></>; }

Keywords: hydration error, server client mismatch, Date, window, useEffect, flicker
Description: If the server and the browser render different text, React throws away the HTML or flashes.
Do: Render the same thing first; read browser-only values after mount.
Don't: Do not read window or the current time during render.
Code Example Good: const [w, setW] = useState(null); useEffect(() => setW(window.innerWidth), []);
Code Example Bad: const w = window.innerWidth; // undefined on the server

Keywords: conditional rendering, 0 renders, short circuit, ternary, null
Description: Writing count && <X /> prints the number 0 when count is zero.
Do: Compare to a boolean or use a ternary.
Don't: Do not short-circuit on a number.
Code Example Good: {items.length > 0 ? <List items={items} /> : null}
Code Example Bad: {items.length && <List items={items} />}

Issue: Keep hidden UI alive with Activity
Keywords: Activity, hidden tab, preserve state, offscreen, prerender
Description: Unmounting a tab loses its state; hiding it with CSS keeps its effects running.
Do: Use Activity in hidden mode to keep state and pause work.
Don't: Do not unmount screens that people switch between often.
Code Example Good: <Activity mode={tab === 'inbox' ? 'visible' : 'hidden'}><Inbox /></Activity>
Code Example Bad: {tab === 'inbox' && <Inbox />}

Keywords: next/image, LCP, priority, width height, sizes, layout shift
Description: Unsized or oversized images delay the main content and push things around.
Do: Use the Image component with dimensions and sizes, and mark the hero image as priority.
Don't: Do not use priority on every image.
Code Example Good:
import Image from 'next/image';
<Image src='/hero.jpg' alt='Workshop' width={1200} height={600} sizes='100vw' priority />

Keywords: next/font, font display, layout shift, FOUT, subset
Description: Fonts fetched late cause a swap that reflows text.
Do: Load fonts through next/font, which self-hosts and sets size-adjusted fallbacks.
Don't: Do not link a font stylesheet in the head by hand.
Code Example Good:
import { Fraunces } from 'next/font/google';
const display = Fraunces({ subsets: ['latin'], display: 'swap' });
Code Example Bad: <link href='https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fraunces' rel='stylesheet' />

Keywords: static, dynamic, cookies, headers, searchParams, route caching
Description: Reading cookies or headers in a route makes the whole thing render per request.
Do: Keep pages static where possible and isolate dynamic reads in a Suspense-wrapped part.
Don't: Do not read cookies in a root layout.
Code Example Good: <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}><CartCount /></Suspense> // CartCount reads cookies
Code Example Bad: // root layout.js: const c = (await cookies()).get('x'); makes every page dynamic

Keywords: loading.js, instant navigation, skeleton, streaming, route segment
Description: Without a loading file, navigation waits for the slowest part before showing anything.
Do: Add a loading file beside the page so the shell appears immediately.
Don't: Do not leave slow segments blank.
Code Example Good:
// app/dashboard/loading.js
export default function Loading() { return <DashboardSkeleton />; }
Code Example Bad: // no loading.js; navigation freezes until all data returns

Keywords: useEffectEvent, effect event, stale value, latest props, subscription
Description: An effect that uses a changing value either goes stale or re-subscribes every time it changes.
Do: Move the non-reactive part into an effect event.
Don't: Do not omit dependencies to hide the problem.
Code Example Good:
const onTick = useEffectEvent(() => log(count));
useEffect(() => { const t = setInterval(onTick, 1000); return () => clearInterval(t); }, []);
Code Example Bad: useEffect(() => { const t = setInterval(() => log(count), 1000); return () => clearInterval(t); }, [count]);

Keywords: useRef, mutable value, no rerender, timer id, previous value
Description: A value that should not cause a render, such as a timer id, belongs in a ref.
Do: Store it in useRef and read or write it in handlers and effects.
Don't: Do not read ref.current during render for display.
Code Example Good:
const timer = useRef(null);
function start() { timer.current = setTimeout(done, 500); }
Code Example Bad: const [timer, setTimer] = useState(null); // render on every start

Keywords: useId, accessibility, label for, ssr id, hydration
Description: A counter or random id differs between server and client and breaks label links.
Do: Use useId for ids shared by a label and its input.
Don't: Do not use Math.random for ids.
Code Example Good:
const id = useId();
<><label htmlFor={id}>Name</label><input id={id} /></>
Code Example Bad: <input id={'f' + Math.random()} />

Keywords: effect chain, cascading render, event handler, derived update
Description: One effect that sets state which triggers another effect creates several renders for one change.
Do: Do the work in the event handler that caused it.
Don't: Do not link state updates through effects.
Code Example Good: function buy() { post('/buy'); setCart([]); showToast(); }
Code Example Bad: useEffect(() => { if (bought) setCart([]); }, [bought]); useEffect(() => { if (!cart.length) showToast(); }, [cart]);

Issue: Use Strict Mode to find impurity
Keywords: StrictMode, double render, pure component, side effects in render
Description: Strict Mode re-runs renders and effects in development to reveal code that is not pure.
Do: Keep it on, and fix mutations and missing cleanups it exposes.
Don't: Do not turn it off to hide a double-fire.
Code Example Good: <StrictMode><App /></StrictMode>
Code Example Bad:
let calls = 0; function Cmp() { calls++; return

{calls}

; }

Keywords: use hook, promise, Suspense, pass promise from server
Description: A server component can start a request and pass the promise to a client one, which reads it with use and suspends.
Do: Create the promise on the server, pass it down, and read it with use inside Suspense.
Don't: Do not create a new promise on every client render.
Code Example Good: function Comments({ commentsPromise }) { const comments = use(commentsPromise); return <List items={comments} />; }
Code Example Bad: function Comments() { const comments = use(fetch('/api/c').then(r => r.json())); }

Keywords: React Compiler, auto memo, babel plugin, manual memo
Description: The React Compiler adds memoisation at build time for components that follow the rules, so hand-written memo calls become mostly noise.
Do: Enable it and keep components pure; keep useMemo only where it is measured to matter.
Don't: Do not scatter memo everywhere in advance.
Code Example Good:
// next.config.js
module.exports = { reactCompiler: true };
Code Example Bad: const a = useMemo(() => 1 + 1, []); const b = useCallback(() => {}, []);
